name: Launch Bay
summary: Hostile leper gnomes and corrupted machines hold Launch Bay, deep in Gnomeregan beyond the Hall of Gears. The underground airfield once served gnomish flying machines and bombers; now the city’s former hangar is under enemy control.

sections.title: A Grounded Airfield
sections.body: Launch Bay’s two tiers once housed Gnomeregan’s aerial fleet. Ramps from the upper walkway lead to a central platform where flying machines and heavy bombers remain parked, left behind before the city was evacuated. Crazed leper gnomes now roam the flight decks, maintaining and guarding the idle war machines in place of skilled pilots.

sections.title: Crossroads of the Deep City
sections.body: Launch Bay also joins several parts of the complex. Ramps from its southeastern corridor descend into the Engineering Labs. On the lower deck, invading Dark Iron dwarves choke the southern passage. That tunnel offers a perilous route toward Tinkers' Court, deep in the city.

faq.q: What is the Launch Bay used for?
faq.answer: Launch Bay was built as an underground airfield and hangar for gnomish flying machines and bombers. Now leper gnomes dwelling in the ruins have taken over the neglected space.

faq.q: Who controls the Launch Bay now?
faq.answer: Leper gnomes and aggressive mechanical contraptions occupy Launch Bay’s upper and lower levels. Near the southern exits, hostile Dark Iron dwarves have also carved out a foothold.

faq.q: Where does the Launch Bay lead?
faq.answer: The upper eastern tunnel leads back to the Hall of Gears. Southeastern ramps descend to the Engineering Labs, while a southern tunnel on the lower deck leads deeper into Gnomeregan toward Tinkers' Court.

faq.q: Are the flying machines here operational?
faq.answer: Several gnomish flying machines and bombers remain parked on the central platforms. They sit idle and untended amid the chaos of the city’s fall.

angles.text: As a gnome, seeing flying machines and bombers abandoned and overrun by irradiated leper kin is a bitter reminder of your city’s tragic loss.
As an engineer, you can see the hangar’s gnomish aeronautics and vehicle chassis up close, though hostile contraptions guard the area.
